items.title: When Should LLM Agents Forget? Memory Filtering Under Query-Critical Resolver Errors
items.summary:

Abstract: LLM memory systems often delete facts classified as stale. We show that this hard-filtering step can reduce downstream accuracy when resolver errors delete query-critical facts. Across three models, a controlled sensitivity intervention moves hard-drop from gains of +0.186 to +0.230 at perfect resolution to losses of -0.176 to -0.181 at the lowest tested reliability. items.reasoning: The paper shows that hard-deleting 'stale' facts from agent memory can hurt accuracy when the resolver misclassifies query-critical facts. Meevo can use this directly when designing its own memory layer over Claude, for example by preferring soft filtering over hard deletion. It does not affect Claude API pricing or capabilities, and users will not expect anything from it.

items.title: Does the Ranking Hold? A Practitioner-Facing Audit of Hallucination Detectors on Small, Quantized, On-Device LLMs
